chunks: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Sindi ibn al-Rabi' from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr from his father from Jamil ibn Darradj from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"When a martyr is killed and only flesh is found without bone, he is not prayed over; but if bone is found without flesh, he is prayed over."

key_terms.صُلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ: he was prayed over (funeral prayer performed)
key_terms.لَمْ يُصَلَّ عَلَيْهِ: he was not prayed over (funeral prayer not performed)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on funeral prayer if the body is reduced to only flesh or only bone?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential criteria for the validity of the funeral prayer based on the physical state of the corpse, specifically distinguishing between the presence of bone and flesh. In Shia fiqh, this ruling highlights that the integrity of the skeletal structure is a primary condition for the prayer, whereas the absence of bone renders the ritual inapplicable. This distinction underscores the practical application of *fiqh* in handling remains during different stages of decomposition or burial.
